analyticalMisses.note: CHC F3 YES lost to a 0-0 tie through 3 despite CHC winning the full game 3-0 -- three-way tie risk on an early-inning team-side horizon.
CHC F5 YES lost to the same 0-0 tie through 5 -- same tie-risk failure mode as the F3 leg, on the same underlying thesis.
MIA F5 YES suffered the same three-way tie problem (0-0 through 5) in a game correctly identified pregame as pitcher-friendly.
Burns under-18-outs NO and under-7-K NO were both premised on a workload-limit thesis that proved incorrect -- Burns threw seven scoreless innings with eight strikeouts.
Burns under-7-K NO -- see above; highly correlated with the outs-18 NO leg, both losing for the same underlying reason.
TB F5 YES over-weighted Bassitt's return-from-injury uncertainty as a performance downgrade; F5 was a 2-2 tie.

analyticalWins.note: Alcantara 19+ outs YES was a strong process win -- he recorded 21 outs (7.0 IP).
AZ-ATL F5 under (NO on over-4.5) was a strong process win, consistent with the pitching matchup; combined F5 runs were 0.
Chris Sale 7+ Ks YES was a strong process win, consistent with the pitching matchup; Sale recorded 9 Ks in 6.0 IP.
WSH F5 was an example of the horizon working correctly: it won through five (1-0) even though Washington lost the full game 4-1.

gameLevelConcentration.note: F3 CHC-YES + F5 CHC-YES on the same early-Cubs-lead thesis; both lost on a 0-0 tie through 5 despite CHC winning 3-0.
F5 MIA-YES, Burns 18+ outs NO, Alcantara 19+ outs YES, Burns 7+ K NO -- four correlated exposures to the same pitching duel.

processErrors.note: F3/F5 three-way team-side bets on the same early-lead thesis do not account for tie-state risk -- CHC F3 + CHC F5 combined for $60 of exposure to the same 'Cubs jump out early' idea and both lost purely to a 0-0 tie through the relevant horizon, despite the Cubs winning the full game 3-0.
Multiple horizons/derivatives on the same team thesis (CHC F3 + CHC F5; MIA F5 + Burns outs NO + Burns K NO) were not treated as one exposure cluster when sizing.
The Burns workload thesis (under-18-outs NO, under-7-K NO) was incorrect and the two legs were highly correlated -- both lost together when Burns threw seven scoreless innings with eight strikeouts.
TB F5 over-weighted Chris Bassitt's return-from-injury uncertainty as an automatic performance downgrade rather than modeling it as genuine uncertainty.

proposedInvestigations.note: Recorded as a research/process finding only -- production betting code (RULES.md/config/rules.json) was NOT modified as part of this import.
proposedInvestigations.proposal: Explicit three-way tie-tax review before any F3/F5 team-side bet.
Same-game/same-thesis correlation cap across horizons and derivatives.
Require concrete usage evidence before applying a workload/injury narrative to a prop thesis.
Hitter projection engine remains research-only pending calibration data.
Future manuals should explicitly compare team F3/F5 YES, opponent NO/synthetic equivalent, tie probability, F5 margin, pitcher derivatives, and full-game alternatives before selecting the expression.
